extracted.intended_audience: United States Indian Agents; Commissioner of Indian Affairs; Department of the Interior officials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for preparing and assessing United States Indian agency annual reports, covering health, agriculture, education, policing, supplies, buildings, treaty implementation, and relations with tribes. Emphasizes measurable outputs (crops, births/deaths, allotments), administrative practices, and recommended interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Indian laborers from employer exploitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must not defraud Indians of their labor or wages; Indians should receive promised wages and in money rather than 'trash'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent intervention is required when employers cheat Indians (example: arresting an employer who paid a man in buck-shot); when potential disputes would reach the agent, employers are more willing to deal honorably. Encourages agents to protect and promote Indians' interests in labor disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary and public health services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide effective medical services through an agency physician; monitor prevalence of diseases (e.g., venereal disease) and report general health status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A resident physician rendered efficient service and reduced disease prevalence, but isolation of some tribes makes full access difficult. Record numbers treated, births, and deaths (examples: number of Indians receiving treatment, births, deaths).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of limited hospital accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish limited hospital arrangements to shelter and subsist sick Indians who travel great distances for treatment and cannot immediately return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request limited hospital accommodations before the rainy season when sickness generally prevails; the cost would be trifling compared with the benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate population and statistical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and submit statistical reports of population by tribe, using best available sources to approximate numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Census/enumeration should be kept current (example: last census taken during annuity issue; subsequent changes recorded) so the agent can present correct statements of numbers and demographic breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of agriculture through stability and infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanent reservation location, agency buildings, and established schools are prerequisites for meaningful progress in agriculture; unsettled conditions hinder farming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until treaties are completed, reservations settled, and agency infrastructure provided, farming progress will be limited. Encourages creating stable conditions (reservation, buildings, schools) before expecting agricultural advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align economic encouragement with land suitability and cultural inclination
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage pastoral pursuits (sheep, cattle, horses) where climate and land favor stock raising rather than forcing unsuited agricultural programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenditure and effort would be better spent inducing stock-raising where the land and Indians' inclinations make it more suitable than tilling soil (example: Southern Utes more suited to pastoralism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify and support agricultural activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Report number of Indians farming, acreage cultivated, crops raised, and provide implements and machinery to support production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: thirty Indians cultivating seventy-five acres producing specific bushels of potatoes, corn, wheat, oats, etc.; recommend breaking new land by contract and supplying mowers, implements to improve yields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage fencing and agency farms
rubrics_metrics.description: Support construction of fences and maintenance of agency farm plots to model cultivation and provide produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report rods of fencing built (example: 160 rods by Indians) and operation of an agency farm (example: one-acre farm near the river) even if agency duties limit farm attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adequate housing and encourage house-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish suitable housing for chiefs and encourage Indians to build and occupy good log houses when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted scarcity of Indian-occupied houses (example: only one house for Chief Ouray) and expressed desire among Indians to have log houses built with their assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education: preference for boarding schools over day schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish boarding schools to educate Indian children away from parental home influences; day schools risk tardiness and absenteeism due to travel distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend boarding school to accommodate ~100 scholars of both sexes; day schools cause failures because parents live 3–25 miles away and influence pupils negatively. Education is of 'greatest importance' and English instruction is urged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly and fair distribution of subsistence rations
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize ration issues to avoid crowding and confusion; use temporary seating and designated distributors who deliver rations by ticket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change from allowing Indians to crowd commissary door to selecting a few Indians to fetch rations using ration tickets produces greater general satisfaction and reduces confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cultural mediation to reform harmful customs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents should use direct communication in the Indians' language and council persuasion to discourage destructive customs (e.g., burning property upon a death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: agent called Chipeta and relatives in council, urged against destruction citing Ouray's wishes and government opposition; successful persuasion considered an 'important point' toward civilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate legitimate selection of tribal leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist tribes in choosing recognized chiefs by explaining selection methods and facilitating voting or councils to produce accepted leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: agent advocated for Sappovonare, explained white method of selecting leaders, had Indians vote by name which resulted in near-unanimous election and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain continuity of agent appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent changes in agents harm Indians' ability to understand and trust the agent; continuity is necessary to achieve governmental objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent agent turnover allows unprincipled whites to foment discontent; a stable agent fosters respect, confidence, and success in advancing Indians' interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt implementation of treaty provisions by government
rubrics_metrics.description: Treaty provisions and government obligations toward Indians should be carried into effect without unnecessary delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent repeatedly urges that treaty promises be executed promptly to maintain trust and secure the benefits contemplated by negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and support Indian police with appropriate compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize a corps of Indian policemen representing bands, provide pay and uniforms, and consider additional compensation for horse use and yearly clothing allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Police were reorganized and paid, uniforms issued; recommended pay increase or horse allowance and two uniform suits yearly to stimulate cleanliness and effectiveness. Limit use where contact with citizens could be unsafe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure quality and timely delivery of supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplies for issue must be of suitable quality and delivered before roads are impassable; late or poor-quality supplies cause privation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted generally good supplies except unsuitable coffee-pots and inferior citizens' clothing; failure to deliver supplies before winter and spring deprived Indians when most needed and produced much privation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient agency buildings and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency must have adequate buildings for storage of supplies and proper quarters for agent and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient buildings were reported; proper accommodation is necessary both for safeguarding supplies and for enabling agents to earn respect and accomplish their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect Indians from corrupting outside influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent unprincipled white persons from associating with Indians, since such individuals corrupt and sow suspicion against agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degraded white men teach profanity and denounce agents as thieves, causing Indians to distrust legitimate authority and hampering civilization efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan security measures for sensitive events (annuity/issue days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate possible outbreaks at annuity issues and arrange for precautionary security measures (e.g., troop positioning) or other protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: requested troops to halt near agency during issue as a precaution; diplomacy and escorting with Indian police may be used when troops unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report health and demographic metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and report counts of medical treatments, births, and deaths to monitor sanitary conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example statistics provided (e.g., number of Indians treated, births and deaths) and noted that resident physicians generally gain confidence and patients follow prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support missionary and industrial/boarding schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with missionary organizations and establish boarding/industrial schools (boys' and girls') to provide vocational and moral instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Saint John's boarding and industrial school for girls conducted successfully; boarding schools can be expanded when facilities allow; employ teachers to staff boys' boarding-school buildings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote allotment in severalty and disestablishment of villages
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage allotments of land in severalty to families to foster independent homes and self-sufficiency; breaking up villages into family allotments will increase demand for implements and improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: allotments made (160-acre and 10-acre plots); agent recommends allotment and individual occupancy as a means toward self-supporting families and increased artificial wants signaling advancement.
